chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn Ahmad from al-Khashab from Ghiyas ibn Kalub from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him)

That two men disputed before the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) regarding an animal which was in both their hands, and each one of them established the proof that it had been established the evidence that it had been bred in his presence, so 'Ali (peace be upon him) made them both swear an oath, so one of them swore and the other refused to swear, so he judged it for the one who swore.

So it was said to him, 'And if it were not in the hand of either of them and they both established the proof?' He said: 'I would make them both swear, so whichever of the two swears and the other shirks, I would give it to the one who swore. And if they both swear, I would give it between them as two halves.'
It was said, 'And if it was in the hand of one of them and they both established the proof?' He said: 'I would judge it for the one who swore, in whose hand it is.'
ai.seo_question: How does Imam Ali (peace be upon him) rule on property disputes when both parties present evidence and one refuses to take an oath?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details Imam al-Sadiq’s (AS) judicial methodology for resolving conflicting ownership claims, emphasizing the primacy of the oath (yamin) as a decisive evidentiary tool when testimonies are equal. It establishes a nuanced hierarchy where possession (qabd) serves as a tie-breaker for the swearer, reflecting the Shia jurisprudential principle that the burden of proof lies with the claimant while the oath resolves the dispute in favor of the possessor who swears. This ruling underscores the practical application of 'al-yamin ma'a al-shahid' (the oath with the witness) in early Islamic courts.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad, from Al Khashab, from Gayas Bin Kuleyb, from Is’haq Bin Ammar,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> that two men disputed to Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> regarding an animal which was in both their hands, and each one of them established the proof that he had bred it in his presence. So Ali<sup>azwj</sup> made both of them to swear an oath. So one of them swore and the other one refuse to swear. So due to it he<sup>asws</sup> judged for the one who swore the oath.

So it was said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Supposing it was not in the hand of any one of them and they both established the proof?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘They would both have to swear an oath. So whichever of the two swear, and the other one shirks from it, it would be made to be for the one who swore. So if both of them were to swear, it would be made to be for both of them together, (its price) in two halves’.
So if it was in the hands of one of the two and they both establish the proof?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> would judge by it to be for the one who swears in whose hand it is’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Khashshab from Ghiyath ibn Kallub from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar who has narrated the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam,

has said that once two men presented their case before Amir al- Mu’minin, Ali, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a stumper in their hand and each presented testimony that it was bred in his facilities. He (the Imam) then asked them to take an oath. One party did not take oath, then he (the Imam) issued a judgment in favor of the one who had taken the oath.

It then was asked, ‘What would have happened if it was not in the hand of anyone of them and both presented testimony?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘I would ask them to take an oath. If one party took the oath and the other refused, the one who took the oath wins the case. If both of them took oath I will make it for them half and half.’

It then was asked, ‘What happens if it is in the hand of one of them and they both present testimony?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘I would issue a judgment in favor of the one who has it in his hand and takes an oath.’”
